correctness.rationale: Class-homogeneity and clipping at two define a faithful 676-state support quotient. Adding the shore and occupied color gives 2808 tagged states, whose full transitions the included verifier enumerates. The finite check proves first periodic entry by time 3, possible full-configuration periods only 1,3,4, and exact generating-polynomial identities for primitive-3 and primitive-4 states. Independent original vertex-level enumeration checks 94,770 configurations and three explicit witnesses. Formal coefficient extraction supplies all-size formulas; finite tests alone are not treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The essential new implication is a threshold-two contact-induced nonmonotone three-cycle existence pattern in shore size, with exact all-size state counts and a three-step sharp bound. The closest indexed threshold-one complete-bipartite theorem changes at a different neighbor threshold and implies none of this nonmonotonicity. The major inspected 1991 foundational paper studies 2D lattice wave/fixation effects, not labelled complete bipartite orbit enumeration. The 2021 higher-threshold paper addresses infinite trees under random initial states. No known directly covering stronger result was found after explicit implication comparisons; a genuine risk from unindexed work remains.
residual_risks: The indexed search can miss a published equivalent exact enumeration, including older technical reports.

value.rationale: A natural change of the cyclic contact threshold causes the existence of 3-cycles to disappear on shore sizes four and five and reappear at six. The all-size sharp entry bound and exact orbit counts distinguish sparse, intermediate and dense populations and yield asymptotic predominance of 3-cycles. This is a structurally motivated nonlinear network-dynamics classification, not a routine finite recalculation.
